html:
The Wiyot, who call themselves Ku'wil, "the people", are a Native American people of Humboldt Bay on the far northern coast of California, around today's Eureka and Arcata. Their language and that of their Yurok neighbours are the only two in California related to the Algonquian languages of the east.

They fished, gathered shellfish and acorns, and hunted around the bay and the lower Eel and Mad rivers. Gold miners and settlers poured in after 1850 with the Gold Rush. In February 1860, after their world renewal ceremony on Tuluwat Island, local settlers killed scores of Wiyot, mostly women, children and elders, in the 1860 Wiyot massacre. The writer Bret Harte, then a local journalist, condemned it and had to leave town. In 2019 the city of Eureka returned most of Tuluwat Island to the Wiyot Tribe. Their neighbours included the Whilkut and the Nongatl.
